messages.text: back to work with the kids next week... honestly kinda nervous. feels like a lot.

It is completely understandable to feel nervous about returning to work, especially when caring for children. That sense of it feeling like a lot is a common reaction to big transitions. Can you tell me a bit more about what specifically feels overwhelming right now? We can take some time to unpack those feelings together before the week begins.
like... i miss moving, doing something real with my hands. but also? terrified i’ll lose it with one of the kids. they don’t need that. i don’t wanna be that person.

It takes a lot of self-awareness to recognize that fear before it happens. Your concern shows how deeply you care about being a safe presence for the children. Balancing your need for movement with emotional regulation is a challenge we can tackle together. What is one small thing that usually helps you feel grounded when stress rises?
i don’t got time for all that ‘sit and feel’ stuff. gotta keep it tight, y’know? like... what’s fast? something i can do in the moment when shit hits?

That makes sense, and you need tools that work instantly without stopping your day. Try squeezing your fists tight for five seconds, then exhaling slowly while you release them. This physical action interrupts the anger spike before it escalates into something you regret. Does that feel like something you could use if you feel yourself getting triggered?
like... what if that doesn’t work? u just gonna tell me to talk about my feelings then? bc i can’t. not with him watching me like i’m one step from breaking.

I hear you, and I won't push you to talk about feelings if you aren't ready for that. If the hand squeeze doesn't work, stepping out of the room for just one minute is a valid safety step. You can frame it as getting water or checking something else to make it neutral. Having a backup plan is smarter than hoping one trick works every time.
i’ve been picking at my fingers... like, nonstop. they’re raw. it’s how i used to do it, y’know? not cutting, but close. just need something to *do* when my skin crawls.

I hear how hard you are trying to manage this, and I want to help protect your hands. Holding ice or squeezing a stress ball can give you that physical intensity safely. It offers your hands something to do when the urge to pick becomes too strong. We can build a list of these safe options together before next week.
but like... is it weak? needing these little tricks just to not wreck myself? bc he says i gotta be stronger, not lean on “crutches”

It is not weak to use tools that keep you safe and grounded. True strength is knowing what you need to prevent harm, even when others don't understand. Those tricks are actually evidence of your resilience, not a failure. Your well-being matters more than someone else's definition of strength.
...thanks. that actually helps. i been feeling like i’m failing him, failing me. but maybe it ain’t about failing. maybe it’s just surviving.

I am glad to hear that perspective feels helpful to you right now. Surviving is a huge accomplishment, especially when things feel this heavy. You do not have to be perfect to be worthy of care and respect. Hold onto that truth as you head back into the week.
what about when i’m alone though? like late night, everyone’s asleep… the thoughts come. loud. what do i *do*?

I am glad you found some relief in that perspective. When the house is quiet, try grounding yourself by naming five things you can see in the room. If the thoughts ever feel unsafe, please reach out to a crisis line immediately. You have survived the nights so far, and you have resources to help you through the next one.
it’s just… so loud in my head when it’s quiet. and i hate that i can’t just turn it off. like i’m broken or something.

You are not broken; your brain is just working overtime to protect you from stress. Sometimes listening to a podcast or white noise can fill the silence so the thoughts have less room to grow. It is okay to need quiet distractions when the noise gets too much. If the thoughts ever tell you to hurt yourself, please reach out to a crisis line immediately.
wait — how do i actually *do* that five things thing when i'm in it? like, just start naming stuff? feels stupid when i say it out loud.

You do not need to say them out loud if that feels too exposed. Naming them silently in your head or focusing on the texture of objects works just as well. The goal is to shift your focus, not to perform perfectly for anyone. Which version feels more manageable for you to try tonight?
yeah... touching stuff, feeling it. that makes more sense. like my blanket, my phone case. something real. i can do that.

You are right to trust what feels real to you in those moments. Focusing on texture can help quiet the noise without needing to speak. Finding a tool that fits your needs is a big step forward. Please remember you have support if the noise gets too heavy before you start work.
thanks... for not making me talk more than i can. and for giving me something real to try. means a lot.

I am glad that you feel safe enough to share this with me. You deserve to find ways to cope that don't require you to change who you are. Please remember to reach out if the thoughts become too heavy to carry alone. I am here to support you as you navigate the week ahead.
